source_text:
Τί οὖν ποιήσωμεν, ἀδελφοί; ἀργήσωμεν ἀπὸ τῆς ἀγαθοποιΐας καὶ ἐγκαταλίπωμεν τὴν ἀγάπην; μηθαμῶς τοῦτο ἐάσαι ὁ δεσπότης ἐφ̓ ἡμῖν γε γενηθῆναι, ἀλλὰ σπεύσωμεν μετὰ ἐκτενείας καὶ προθυμίας πᾶς ἔργον ἀγαθὸν ἐπιτελεῖν.
αὐτὸς γὰρ ὁ δημιουργὸς καὶ δεσπότης τῶν ἁπάντων ἐπὶ τοῖς ἔργοις αὐτοῦ ἀγαλλιᾶται.
τῷ γὰρ παμμεγεθεστάτῳ αὐτοῦ κράτει οὐρανοὺς ἐστήρισεν καὶ τῇ ἀκαταλήπτῳ αὐτοῦ συνέσει διεκόσμησεν αὐτούς: γῆν τε διεχώρισεν ἀπὸ τοῦ περιέχοντος αὐτὴν ὕδατος καὶ ἥδρασεν ἐπὶ τὸν ἀσφαλῆ τοῦ ἰδίου βουλήματος θεμέλιον: τά τε ἐν αὐτῇ ζῶα φοιτῶντα τῇ ἑαυτοῦ διατάξει ἐκέλευσεν εἶναι: θάλασσαν καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ ζῶα προετοιμάσας ἐνέκλεισεν τῇ ἑαυτοῦ δυνάμει.
ἐπὶ πᾶσι τὸ ἐξοχώτατον καὶ παμμέγεθες κατὰ διάνοιαν, ἄνθρωπον, ταῖς ἱεραῖς καὶ ἀμώμοις χερσὶν ἔπλασεν τῆς ἑαυτοῦ εἰκόνος χαρακτῆρα.
οὕτως γάρ φησιν ὁ θεός: Ποιήσωμεν ἄνθρωπον κατ’ εἰκόνα καὶ καθ̓ ὁμοίωσιν ἡμετέραν: καὶ ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν ἄνθρωπον, ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ ἐποίησεν αὐτούς.
ταῦτα οὖν πάντα τελειώσας ἐπῄνεσεν αὐτὰ καὶ ηὐλόγησεν καὶ εἶπεν: Αὐξάνεσθε καὶ πληθύνεσθε.
ἴδωμεν, ὅτι ἐν ἔργοις ἀγαθοῖς πάντες ἐκοσμήθησαν οἱ δίκαιοι, καὶ αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ κύριος ἔργοις ἀγαθοῖς ἑαυτὸν κοσμήσας ἐχάρη.
ἔχοντες οὖν τοῦτον τὸν ὑπογραμμὸν ἀόκνως προσέλθωμεν τῷ θελήματι αὐτοῦ: ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ἰσχύος ἡμῶν ἐργασώμεθα ἔργον δικαιοσύνης.
thought_title: Doing good works eagerly, since God rejoices in his works
orientation: The Roman church, having shown that justification comes through faith and God's will, now urges the Corinthians not to slacken from doing good but to imitate God the Creator, who rejoiced in his own good works.
pass_a_gloss: What therefore shall we do, brothers? Shall we be idle from the doing of good and shall we abandon love? By no means may the Master allow this to happen among us, but let us hasten with earnestness and eagerness to complete every good work. For the Creator himself and Master of all things rejoices over his works. For by his all-greatest might he fixed the heavens and by his incomprehensible understanding he ordered them; and the earth he separated from the water surrounding it and set it upon the secure foundation of his own will; and the living creatures walking about in it he commanded to be by his own arrangement; the sea and the living creatures in it, having prepared beforehand, he shut in by his own power. Above all, the most excellent and all-great in thought, man, with his holy and blameless hands he formed, the imprint of his own image. For thus says God: Let us make man according to our image and likeness; and God made man, male and female he made them. All these things therefore having completed, he praised them and blessed them and said: Increase and multiply. Let us see that in good works all the righteous were adorned, and the Lord himself, having adorned himself with good works, rejoiced. Having therefore this pattern, let us approach his will without shrinking; with all our strength let us work the work of righteousness.

choices.why: Keeps the noun phrase literal and distinct from 'good works' (ἔργον ἀγαθόν) later in the section
Renders the superlative literally to preserve the emphatic size language
Standard rendering for what cannot be grasped by the mind
Literal sense of a stamped mark, emphasizing man as the exact impression of God's image
Captures the negative of hesitation or reluctance in the adverb
Literal sense of a writing-copy or outline to be followed

bible_refs.note: Ποιήσωμεν ἄνθρωπον κατ’ εἰκόνα καὶ καθ’ ὁμοίωσιν ἡμετέραν
καὶ ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν ἄνθρωπον, ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ ἐποίησεν αὐτούς

pass_b_english: What then should we do, brothers? Should we stop doing good and abandon love? May the Master never allow this to happen among us. Instead, let us hasten with earnestness and eagerness to complete every good work.
For the Creator and Master of all things rejoices in his works.

By his all-greatest power he fixed the heavens, and by his incomprehensible understanding he ordered them. He separated the earth from the water surrounding it and set it on the secure foundation of his own will. The living creatures that move upon it he commanded to exist by his own arrangement. The sea and the creatures in it he prepared beforehand and enclosed by his own power.
Above all, he formed with his holy and blameless hands man, most excellent and vast in mind, as the imprint of his own image.
For God says this: “Let us make man according to our image and likeness.” And God made man; male and female he made them (Genesis 1:26-27).
When he had completed all these things, he praised them and blessed them and said, “Increase and multiply” (Genesis 1:28).
Let us see that all the righteous were adorned with good works, and the Lord himself, adorning himself with good works, rejoiced.
Since we have this pattern, let us approach his will without shrinking. With all our strength let us work the work of righteousness.

polish.changed: Clarified the subject of each action (God as Creator and Master), smoothed sentence flow, and made the sequence of creation and the scriptural quotations easier to follow aloud while preserving every claim and reference.

problems.quote: the most excellent and all-greatest being in thought, man
problems.why: 'All-greatest being in thought' is opaque; means 'greatest of created beings.'
problems.fix: Revise to: 'the most excellent of created beings, man.'

edits.old: the most excellent and all-greatest being in thought, man
edits.new: the most excellent of created beings, man

problems.quote: the most excellent of created beings, man
problems.source_quote: τὸ ἐξοχώτατον καὶ παμμέγεθες κατὰ διάνοιαν, ἄνθρωπον
problems.why: Drops that man is also immensely great in mind, not only most excellent.
problems.fix: Above all he formed with his holy and blameless hands man, most excellent and vast in mind, the imprint of his own image.
problems.ruling: Source has two adjectives: τὸ ἐξοχώτατον καὶ παμμέγεθες κατὰ διάνοιαν. English gives only 'most excellent of created beings' and drops παμμέγεθες 'exceedingly great' and κατὰ διάνοιαν 'in mind/intellect'.

edits.old: Above all, he formed with his holy and blameless hands the most excellent of created beings, man, as the imprint of his own image.
edits.new: Above all, he formed with his holy and blameless hands man, most excellent and vast in mind, as the imprint of his own image.

fixed: Restored omission of παμμέγεθες κατὰ διάνοιαν: 'most excellent of created beings' -> 'man, most excellent and vast in mind'.

last_rejected.why: English 'For God says this' loses the quotation formula marking divine speech per voices brief; 'For God says' or 'the holy word says' preferred.
last_rejected.ruling: 'God says this' correctly renders οὕτως γάρ φησιν ὁ θεός; 'this' reflects οὕτως and marks the quotation adequately.

last_rejected.why: Glossary does not include δικαιοσύνη, so no fixed term violated. 'Righteousness' is standard rendering. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: Report itself confirms no glossary violation; 'righteousness' is standard for δικαιοσύνης. No error.
